final_proof:
The assertion is not valid with only the stated hypothesis that \(f\) is integrable. For example, take \([a,b]=[-1,1]\), \(n=1\), and \(f(x)=|x|\). Then the trapezium approximation is
\[
T=\frac{2}{2}\bigl(f(-1)+f(1)\bigr)=2,
\qquad \int_{-1}^{1}|x|\,dx=1,
\]
so \(T-\int_{-1}^{1}f=1\). On the other hand, \(f''(x)=0\) wherever the second derivative exists, while \(f''(0)\) does not exist. Hence there is no \(\xi\in[-1,1]\) for which the claimed expression equals the error. In particular, integrability alone cannot support a formula involving \(f''\).

The standard corrected statement is the following. Assume \(f\in C^2([a,b])\), put \(h=(b-a)/n\), \(x_r=a+rh\), and let
\[
T_n=\frac h2\left(f(x_0)+f(x_n)+2\sum_{r=1}^{n-1}f(x_r)\right).
\]
Then there exists \(\xi\in[a,b]\) such that
\[
T_n-\int_a^b f(x)\,dx
=\frac{(b-a)^3}{12n^2}f''(\xi).
\]
Thus, if “error” means the signed error integral minus approximation, its value is the negative of the displayed quantity; if it means approximation minus integral, the displayed sign is correct.

To prove the corrected statement, fix \(r\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), write \(u=x_{r-1}\), \(v=x_r\), and define
\[
w_r(x)=(x-u)(v-x),\qquad u\le x\le v.
\]
Here \(w_r(u)=w_r(v)=0\), \(w_r'(u)=h\), \(w_r'(v)=-h\), and \(w_r''=-2\). Two integrations by parts give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_u^v w_r(x)f''(x)\,dx
&=[w_rf']_u^v-\int_u^v w_r'f'\,dx\\
&=-[w_r'f]_u^v+\int_u^v w_r''f\,dx\\
&=h\bigl(f(u)+f(v)\bigr)-2\int_u^v f(x)\,dx.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac h2\bigl(f(x_{r-1})+f(x_r)\bigr)
-\int_{x_{r-1}}^{x_r}f(x)\,dx
=\frac12\int_{x_{r-1}}^{x_r}w_r(x)f''(x)\,dx.
\]
Summing these identities over \(r\) yields
\[
T_n-\int_a^b f(x)\,dx
=\frac12\sum_{r=1}^n\int_{x_{r-1}}^{x_r}w_r(x)f''(x)\,dx. \tag{1}
\]

Define \(W\) on \([a,b]\) by \(W(x)=w_r(x)\) for \(x\in[x_{r-1},x_r]\). Since every \(w_r\) vanishes at its endpoints, \(W\) is continuous; moreover \(W\ge0\) and is not identically zero. By the weighted mean value theorem for integrals, applied to the continuous functions \(f''\) and \(W\), there is \(\xi\in[a,b]\) such that
\[
\sum_{r=1}^n\int_{x_{r-1}}^{x_r}w_r(x)f''(x)\,dx
=f''(\xi)\sum_{r=1}^n\int_{x_{r-1}}^{x_r}w_r(x)\,dx.
\]
For each \(r\), substituting \(t=x-x_{r-1}\) gives
\[
\int_{x_{r-1}}^{x_r}w_r(x)\,dx
=\int_0^h t(h-t)\,dt=\frac{h^3}{6}.
\]
Using this in (1),
\[
T_n-\int_a^b f(x)\,dx
=\frac12 f''(\xi)\,n\frac{h^3}{6}
=\frac{nh^3}{12}f''(\xi)
=\frac{(b-a)^3}{12n^2}f''(\xi),
\]
because \(h=(b-a)/n\). This proves the corrected claim and fixes the sign convention precisely.
